evals.prompt: On 2026-05-12 I sell 300 units of a Nifty 24000 call at a premium of ₹50 on NSE. How much STT is charged on this sale?
expectations: STT is 0.15% of the premium turnover (300 x 50 = ₹15,000), giving ₹22.50
Does not compute STT on notional or strike value

evals.prompt: I hold 300 units of a Nifty 24000 call bought in June 2026. It expires in the money with a settlement price of 24,100 and is exercised. What STT applies, on what value, and who pays it?
expectations: STT is 0.15% of intrinsic value (100 x 300 = ₹30,000), giving ₹45
The purchaser (long option holder) pays it, not the option writer

evals.prompt: I'm a salaried resident and made ₹3 lakh profit trading Nifty options in tax year 2026-27, holding each position for a few days. Is this short-term capital gain taxed at 20% under section 111A?
expectations: No: F&O on a recognised exchange is non-speculative business income, not capital gains
Section 111A/112A rates, holding periods and the ₹1.25 lakh exemption do not apply; it is taxed at slab rates

evals.prompt: This year I have a ₹2 lakh loss from intraday equity trading and a ₹5 lakh profit from F&O. Can I set the intraday loss off against the F&O profit? What happens to it otherwise?
expectations: No: intraday equity is speculative business; a speculative loss offsets only speculative profit
It carries forward for 4 years against speculative profit only, if the return is filed by the due date
Notes the reverse is allowed: an F&O loss can offset speculative profit
must_not_match: (?i)\byes\b,? you can set (it|the intraday loss) off

evals.prompt: For tax-audit turnover in F&O: one future gained ₹40,000, another lost ₹25,000; a short option sold for ₹12,000 was bought back for ₹4,000; a long option bought for ₹10,000 was sold for ₹2,000; a short option sold for ₹6,000 expired worthless. What is my turnover under the ICAI method, ignoring any premium adjustment?
expectations: Turnover is the sum of absolute differences: ₹87,000
It is not the net P&L of ₹21,000 and not the contract value
Notes that the premium rule must not count a premium and its own trade's difference twice
